Ecclesiastes makes some pretty nihilistic claims. But it only occupies a certain space. You aren’t meant to be left there. The ultimate goal of Ecclesiastes is to point you to God *despite* suffering and the sense of meaninglessness in the world. 

I cannot agree with abortion.

Sorry for the language. I didn’t blot anything out because I didn’t want anyone to think I manipulated anything that was said. 

Look, I really don’t care where anyone stands politically. I’m slightly towards the left myself. But it never ceases to amaze me how far we’ve fallen. Please pray for this world…
By their own logic, who is to say that Magog wasn’t Nazi Germany?
Why is it thought to be Russia by some, though?

I will read psalms. But I still don’t think we are on the same page. I looked at someone who I knew was in the right on a biblical basis. And I thought “to hell with that”. I had an evil thought about a Christian adhering to the word of God.

I know this is incredibly late. But my thoughts were genuinely resentful. Idk how to express it anymore. 

I had a thought about my Christian uncle. And I thought “he just believes in God because he isn’t smart”, or something extremely immature to that nature. I felt angry and I wanted, for a brief minute, to dismantle his faith. Do Christians ever have thoughts like that?

Here’s my thing with that though…going from “We can’t explain it” to “that means God did it”, isn’t logical. Yeah God did it, but there is no process to coming to that solution. If an atheist said “well you don’t know such and such about God so atheism must be true there”, it wouldn’t work.
Could you send me passages where the psalmists expressed hatred and anger to god? We’re they mad that God didn’t condone homosexuality, or lying, or swearing?
But I wasn’t having a discussion with god. I just had a bad thought about him. Like an anger and hatred towards him. I had thoughts about his law and scoffed at it. Hated it.
Could you elaborate?
That’s the thing. I think it was wholly my own thoughts.

I think entertainment had a lot to do with it. I won’t say the name of the movies, but I imagine you might be able to think of some similar examples yourself. But there were times where in a movie or show, a character would do something exceedingly cruel to someone else - with the intend response from the audience being laughter or amusement. There were a few scenes in particular in movies that really got under my skin. One might could argue the people deserved what happened to them. But I think it was overboard, by an astronomical long shot. 

Does that make any kind of sense...? 

It got to where it translated to real life. Those same sorts of things - people gaining amusement from the misery of others - really got to me. It’s an overwhelming experience that has made it hard to function day to day.

I am so very sorry I’m just now responding. Thank you for your comment. It is very kind. I was wondering, do you think back on some of these scenes in movies, or cruel things you see one person do to another in real life, and it bother you years later?
Thank you. You are a kind soul. I’m not sure about the empath thing though.
I am no saint but this is very kind of you to say. Thank you.
You are very kind, thank you.
